highlights_headline: SkiaSharp 4.156.0 adds GTK4 GPU rendering and Uno 7 support while tightening native lifetimes and platform requirements.
highlights_body: The Skia m156 line restores Linux NoDependencies font discovery, paces Android texture rendering to display refresh and updates .NET 11 WebAssembly assets. Review the Apple, Tizen, Uno, pixel-scaling and input-validation migrations before upgrading.

breaking.title: Raise Apple deployment targets
breaking.body: SkiaSharp and HarfBuzzSharp native libraries now require macOS 12 and iOS, tvOS and Mac Catalyst 15, with managed minima aligned. Raise application deployment targets accordingly; a lower native minimum from an earlier preview does not override higher framework requirements. Existing .NET 9 targets remain.

breaking.title: Target Tizen 10
breaking.body: Tizen native assets now target net10.0-tizen10.0 and require Tizen 10; the new packages do not support Tizen 8 or 9. Retarget applications and manifests to Tizen 10. Native source builds require GCC 14.2 and support x64 and arm64.

breaking.title: Move Uno integrations to Uno 7
breaking.body: Non-Windows Uno views now require Uno 7 and .NET 10. SKSwapChainPanel derives from Grid, drops RaiseOnUnsupported and uses a CPU canvas with null GRContext; use SKCanvasElement for GPU rendering. Migrate pre-Uno 7 WasmShell pipelines to the .NET SDK WebAssembly path. Windows facades retain the WinAppSDK control.

breaking.title: Choose GTK4 logical coordinates explicitly
breaking.body: SKDrawingArea now paints in physical pixels by default on high-density displays, matching the new SKGLArea. Set IgnorePixelScaling=true to retain logical paint coordinates while keeping full-resolution backing pixels. RawInfo remains physical and GTK input coordinates remain logical.

breaking.title: Pass well-formed encoded font buffers
breaking.body: Encoded font operations now reject negative byte lengths with ArgumentOutOfRangeException and odd GlyphId byte counts with ArgumentException. Supply nonnegative lengths and complete 16-bit glyph IDs to BreakText, glyph conversion, counting, measurement and text-path operations. Encoded BreakText results count bytes; string and char-span results count UTF-16 code units.

breaking.title: Keep SKData copy lengths within the source array
breaking.body: SKData.CreateCopy(byte[], ulong) now throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException when the requested length exceeds the array. Pass a length within the source array rather than relying on an out-of-bounds native read.

breaking.title: Pass one encoding unit to StringUtilities
breaking.body: GetUnicodeCharacterCode validates encoded byte width: use Utf8 only for ASCII, Utf16 for a single BMP character and Utf32 for supplementary characters. Multi-unit input throws ArgumentException rather than being partially decoded. GetString(byte[], encoding) now throws ArgumentNullException, not NullReferenceException, for null input.

bullets.detail: Updates the renderer to milestone 156 without managed API additions from the engine bump. HarfBuzzSharp's 14.4.0.100 package revision still uses the HarfBuzz 14.4.0 engine.

Adds SKGLArea with PaintSurface, CanvasSize, GRContext and an opt-in render loop. GTK owns the GL context; use QueueRender to invalidate. Both GTK4 views support IgnorePixelScaling, and manually bundled GTK runtimes must include the libepoxy dispatcher.

Restores directory-backed system-font discovery for Linux NoDependencies packages, using /usr/share/fonts/ by default. Family lookup and SKShaper can use installed fonts again without adding a fontconfig dependency; explicitly loaded fonts remain supported.

Automatic GLTextureView and MAUI Android SKGLView render loops follow Choreographer display callbacks rather than swap throughput. Explicit render requests remain independent, rendering stays on the GL worker, and pause, resize and reattachment retain lifecycle progress.

Rejects overflowing shader slot counts and invalid runtime-effect types, budgets region storage for subdivided conics, and contains failed partial runtime-shader pipelines rather than executing unresolved branches.

Corrects unsupported GLES BGRA-as-RGBx uploads, Graphite hairline and subpixel stroke bounds, and full paint-key comparisons. Adds glyph-bounds and distance-field allocation guards, and fixes inverse-filled Graphite shapes outside the scissor.

Binds internal HarfBuzz function calls to the bundled Linux implementation, preventing global system HarfBuzz exports loaded by GTK from mixing incompatible private objects. Normal and NoDependencies Linux builds inherit the correction.

Uses the correct native boolean widths for Skia and HarfBuzz callbacks while retaining public managed bool signatures, including false-returning font callbacks. Also corrects optional native stream callbacks and XPS COM ownership.

bullets.lead: Bounded Windows font and view lifetimes
bullets.detail: DWriteCore custom fonts use isolated factories so application font data can be released after the last dependent typeface clone is disposed. EGL teardown unbinds this view's current context before destroying its surface, releasing the native window instead of retaining the panel.

Disposing SKFrontBufferedManagedStream clears its reference to a borrowed wrapped stream even when disposeUnderlyingStream is false. It does not dispose that borrowed stream; the caller remains responsible for disposal.

Valid managed pixel copies avoid an intermediate SKData allocation while preserving native validation for invalid inputs. HarfBuzzSharp pools UTF-32 string encoding and avoids a native feature-string allocation without changing decoding semantics.

Selects Emscripten 6.0.2 archives for .NET 11; .NET 8 keeps 3.1.34 and .NET 9/10 keep 3.1.56. Bundles WebGPU C++ support inside libSkiaSharp.a so application C sources no longer receive incompatible C++ flags; JavaScript glue remains a link input.

Aligns library dependencies with Windows App SDK 1.7.250909003 and updates ANGLE to chromium/8118, retaining declared Windows runtime minima. The fork-specific WinRT target is retired; desktop Windows, Windows App SDK/WinUI and Nano Server remain supported.

contributor_summaries.ramezgerges: Restored Linux NoDependencies font discovery, bundled WebGPU C++ support and rebuilt Uno views for Uno 7.
contributor_summaries.akoeplinger: Disabled duplicate Azure DevOps dependency automation and corrected GitOps author mentions.
contributor_summaries.VirgilMing: Fixed Linux HarfBuzz symbol preemption and made Blazor CPU sample captures wait for the first paint.
contributor_summaries.dalexsoto: Updated contextual scan dispositions and terminology without changing product behavior.
contributor_summaries.rolfbjarne: Removed unused sample files to reduce automated scanning noise.

preview_summaries.v4.156.0-preview.1.26512.10: Introduced Skia m156, GTK4 GPU rendering and physical-pixel scaling, and restored Linux NoDependencies font discovery. Also aligned .NET 11 WebAssembly assets and raised Tizen packages to Tizen 10.
preview_summaries.v4.156.0-rc.1.26553.11: Added Uno 7 support and display-paced Android rendering, and corrected font, stream, callback and GPU lifetimes. Raised Apple minimums to macOS 12 and iOS/tvOS/Catalyst 15, tightened input validation and fixed Linux HarfBuzz symbol preemption.

harfbuzz_summary: Fixes Linux symbol preemption and native callback boolean widths, pools UTF-32 encoding and reduces feature-string allocation. WebAssembly assets follow the .NET 11 Emscripten 6.0.2 mapping, and Apple native libraries require macOS 12 or iOS/tvOS/Catalyst 15. Native HarfBuzz remains 14.4.0.

v4.156.0-preview.1.26512.10.headline: Preview 1 introduces Skia m156, GTK4 GPU rendering and restored Linux NoDependencies font discovery.
v4.156.0-preview.1.26512.10.body: GTK4 painting now defaults to physical pixels; enable IgnorePixelScaling for logical coordinates. WebAssembly assets align with .NET 11, and Tizen packages require Tizen 10.

v4.156.0-rc.1.26553.11.headline: The release candidate adds Uno 7 support and corrects font, stream and callback lifetimes.
v4.156.0-rc.1.26553.11.body: It also paces Android rendering to display refresh, tightens input validation and corrects Linux HarfBuzz symbol preemption. Apple libraries now require macOS 12 or iOS, tvOS and Mac Catalyst 15.
